Even k give minimum 4L², odd k give L²+4y²; hence λ²=L²+min(3L²,4y²). Uniform transverse y gives X=min(1,Q²), Q uniform [0,H/(sqrt3 L)]. Exact integrations yield both W branches; the polynomial (9r−10)²(27r²+60r+100)/(7500r⁴) proves unique maximum at 10/9 and the 1/10 atom. Independently checked 117 deck distances and six exact rational moments/deficits. Boundaries and nonprimitive classes are properly included; calculations not substituted for proof.
residual_risks: No generalization to curved/embedded bands. Boundary basepoints have area zero, and shortest based loops need not be smooth periodic geodesics.
